summary: Input facade over the classic Input Manager, using Unity's default axis and button names.
overview: One place to ask for movement, look and buttons, backed by the classic Input Manager. It uses Unity's stock axis names (Horizontal, Vertical, Mouse X/Y, Fire1, Jump) so it works with no project setup at all.

It is a standalone ALTERNATIVE to NewInputSystemManager, not a runtime-swappable backend. Add whichever matches your project's input setting rather than switching between them, so neither depends on Active Input Handling being set to "Both".
useCases: A project on the classic Input Manager that wants gameplay code free of Input.GetAxis calls.
Prototyping where installing and configuring the Input System package is not worth it yet.
Keeping a single call site to swap later, by replacing the component rather than editing callers.

gotchas.title: An unknown axis or button name throws in Unity
gotchas.body: Queries are routed through a guard so a missing name does not take the game down, but the input simply never fires — check the Input Manager if a button seems dead.

gotchas.title: Requires Active Input Handling to include the old manager
gotchas.body: With the project set to "Input System Package (New)" only, every query returns nothing. That is the setting to check first.
